newsitem.title: USA: "First Wives Club" leads pack at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "First Wives Club" leads pack at U.S. box office.

text.p: "The First Wives Club" restored some vigour to an anaemic U.S. box office by opening at the top of the heap with an estimated gross of $19.1 million, according to studio estimates Sunday.

The movie smashed the September opening record of $13.9 million attained by "Seven" last year and is also the top grossing No. 1 since July 19-21 when "Independence Day" earned $21.27 million in its fourth weekend.
Goldie Hawn, Diane Keaton and Bette Midler star in the movie as women who seek revenge on their husbands after being dumped for younger women.

It also left the rest of the field in the dust. Bruce Willis' "Last Man Standing" opened in second with $7.1 million, while "Fly Away Home" slipped a notch to third in its second weekend with $3.8 million. Last week's No. 1, "Maximum Risk", fell to fourth with $3.0 million.

Not surprisingly, "The First Wives Club" attracted a strong female audience, according to Barry London, deputy chairman of Paramount Pictures, which released the film. "But we are getting a strong mix of what I call the date night crowd," he added.
Paramount, a unit of Viacom Inc. will release the movie in Germany, Britain and Australia later this year, and in the rest of the world at the beginning of 1997, he said.

Meanwhile, the studio plans to increase the number of North American screens by several hundred next weekend from ths current 1,922. The movie averaged a rousing $9,886 per screen, the highest in the top 10.

Among new movies in limited release, the gourmet movie "Big Night" opened with $172,214 from 12 screens, giving it an average of $14,351. "Surviving Picasso", in which Sir Anthony Hopkins plays the Spanish artist, generated $87,000 from three screens for an average of $29,000.
